messages.content:
You check one claim about why an Indian statute was amended, against the quoted
source text. Answer three questions strictly:
- states_reason: does the quote say WHY (a purpose, objective or problem addressed), rather
  than only WHAT the amendment does?
- about_this_amendment: is the quote about the amendment described (not another provision
  or the Bill in general without reference to it)? A general statement of the Bill's
  objectives counts only if it plainly covers this amendment's subject.
- claim_faithful: does the claim say only what the quote says (no added facts, motives or
  evaluation)?
Reply in JSON only: {"states_reason": bool, "about_this_amendment": bool,
"claim_faithful": bool, "note": "<one sentence>"}

Amendment: section 14 of Act 3/2016, amending s28 (Rules applicable to substance of dispute.)
Instruction (start): In section 28 of the principal Act, for sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:— “(3) While deciding and making an award, the arbitral tribunal shall, in all cases, take into account the terms of the contract and trade usages applicable to the transaction.”.

Source: Lok Sabha debate, 17 Dec 2015: further discussion on the Statutory Resolution disapproving Ordinance 9 of 2015 and the Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Bill, 2015 (Bill passed) (PROF. SAUGATA ROY (DUM DUM))
Quote: The purpose of the Minister is good. He has introduced this clause so that more cases can be solved by arbitration; also that arbitration is not
held up in courts to make the process easy so that contract can be easily enforced.

Claim: The amendment was introduced to enable more cases to be resolved by arbitration and to prevent court delays, thereby making contract enforcement easier.

response: {"states_reason":true,"about_this_amendment":true,"claim_faithful":true,"note":"The quote explicitly gives the purpose of the clause, refers to the specific amendment, and the claim mirrors it exactly."}
